evidence_summary: Solid early engineering employment after college is documented, but the distinctive public milestones (flight software leadership on major space missions; NFL referee) occurred decades later. Ordinary post-grad employment is not coded as a material ≤26 breakout.

name: Erik Meijer

Born April 29, 1958; first job ~1981 (~age 23) at Cherry Lane Music mail-order; 'helping found' U.S. MacUser (1984, age ~26) and later MacWarehouse (~1985, age ~27) predate Netflix (1997–98, age ~39–40). early_history_summary: Born Chappaqua, New York, to Jewish family (father nuclear engineer/financial adviser; mother real estate firm operator; Bernays/Freud family connections). Hamilton College geology degree; direct-mail and magazine/mail-order software marketing career (MacUser, MacWarehouse, Borland) before co-founding Netflix with Reed Hastings.
family_context_summary: Raised in Chappaqua, NY; father Stephen Bernays Randolph (Austrian-born nuclear engineer turned financial adviser); mother Muriel Lipchik ran a real estate firm. Related to Edward Bernays and Sigmund Freud via paternal line.
parent_family_domain_summary: Professional/entrepreneurial household with engineering and real-estate backgrounds and notable public-relations ancestry; not a direct tech-startup apprenticeship, but resources and status were present.
evidence_summary: Early marketing/mail-order experience by mid-20s is real but not treated as the material breakout; Netflix founding CEO role and industry-transforming company occurred ~age 39–40. Conservative eligibility bar excludes forcing MacUser involvement as the ≤26 milestone.

evidence_summary: Strong graduate path with MS by ~24, but PhD and field-defining testing contributions post-26. Degrees alone are not coded as the required material breakout.

name: Jack Elton Bresenham
milestone_by_age_26: While working in IBM's San Jose computation lab, invented Bresenham's line algorithm for efficient integer-arithmetic raster line drawing on a Calcomp plotter attached to an IBM 1401; in production use by summer 1962 at age 24, becoming one of the earliest foundational algorithms in computer graphics.
early_history_summary: Born October 11, 1937, in Clovis, New Mexico. Earned BSEE from University of New Mexico (1959) and MSIE from Stanford (1960), then joined IBM. Developed the line algorithm at IBM San Jose in 1962; completed Ph.D. at Stanford (1964) and published the method in IBM Systems Journal (1965). Spent 27 years at IBM, retiring as Senior Technical Staff Member in 1987, then taught computer science at Winthrop University for 16 years.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace Clovis, New Mexico.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IBM San Jose, Stanford, early plotter hardware, integer-constrained graphics
evidence_summary: Bresenham combined strong early EE/CS training (UNM, Stanford) with immediate placement at IBM San Jose during the early 1960s computing frontier. Access to scarce plotter/1401 hardware and the need for multiplication-free control code produced a still-standard line algorithm at age 24. Family background is undocumented; the decisive stack was institutional access plus era-specific hardware constraints rather than inherited capital or audience.
starting_point: Born October 11, 1937, in Clovis, New Mexico; early family class and parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Living computer graphics pioneer; retired after 27 years at IBM (Senior Technical Staff Member) and subsequent faculty career at Winthrop University; algorithm remains a standard taught method for raster line drawing.

trajectory.event: Earned BSEE from the University of New Mexico.
Completed MSIE at Stanford and joined IBM.
Developed Bresenham's line algorithm at IBM San Jose; in production use on a Calcomp plotter by summer 1962.
Published 'Algorithm for computer control of a digital plotter' in IBM Systems Journal.
Retired from IBM after 27 years as Senior Technical Staff Member.
Continued recognition as computer-graphics pioneer after multi-year faculty career at Winthrop University.
